q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of brake pads or brake shoes?
title: Brake pad carbon footprint per set
short: Weigh the steel backing plates and each friction material ingredient per set and multiply by supplier figures. Add mixing, hot pressing, curing ovens, grinding, painting and packing energy, then divide plant energy by sets passed.
audience: Brake pad and shoe makers for vehicles

ul: Steel backing plates, often the largest single weight.
Friction mix: fibres, resins, fillers, metal powders and abrasives.
Hot pressing and post-curing ovens, on electricity or gas.

p: Report per set by part number, since a car set and a truck set differ many times over in weight.

example.title: Worked example: brake pad plant per set (one month)
lines: Plant total: 57,900 / 100,000 = 0.579 kg CO2 per set
Add backing plates and friction materials for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
